facts: Gradient and angle of inclination are linked by $m = \tan\theta$, where $0^{\circ} \le \theta < 180^{\circ}$.
A positive gradient gives an acute angle, and $\theta = \tan^{-1}(m)$.
A vertical line has $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ and no gradient.

Exact values: $m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ gives $30^{\circ}$, $m = 1$ gives $45^{\circ}$, $m = \sqrt{3}$ gives $60^{\circ}$, $m = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ gives $150^{\circ}$, $m = -1$ gives $135^{\circ}$, and $m = -\sqrt{3}$ gives $120^{\circ}$.

development.question_text: Find the angle of inclination of the tangent to $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 - 2x$ at $x = 1$.
Find the angle of inclination of the tangent to $y = x^3 - x$ at $x = 2$, correct to the nearest minute.
Find the angle of inclination of the tangent to $y = 4 - x^2$ at its positive $x$-intercept $(2, 0)$, correct to the nearest minute.
Find the coordinates of the two points on the curve $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 - 3x + 1$ where the tangent has an angle of inclination of $45^{\circ}$.
development.solution_text:
$m = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1$
$f'(x) = x^2 - 3$
$x^2 - 3 = 1$
$x^2 = 4$
$x = 2 \text{ or } x = -2$
For $x = 2$: $y = \dfrac{1}{3}(2)^3 - 3(2) + 1 = \dfrac{8}{3} - 6 + 1 = -\dfrac{7}{3} \implies \left(2, -\dfrac{7}{3}\right)$
For $x = -2$: $y = \dfrac{1}{3}(-2)^3 - 3(-2) + 1 = -\dfrac{8}{3} + 6 + 1 = \dfrac{13}{3} \implies \left(-2, \dfrac{13}{3}\right)$
The points are $\left(2, -\dfrac{7}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-2, \dfrac{13}{3}\right)$.
